cards.text: God's been teaching Israel how His people are to live, and now He gives Moses, Israel's leader, another message to pass on. No small talk. He opens with who's talking: "I am the LORD your God."

Then God names two lands whose practices Israel must NOT follow: the one they used to live in, and the one He's bringing them into. That's like moving to a new house and hearing, "Don't bring the old neighborhood's habits with you, and DON'T pick up the new neighborhood's either."

cards.question: God says don't follow the practices of the land Israel used to live in, or of the land He's bringing them into. Which two lands are they?
So how DOES Israel live? Not Egypt's way and not Canaan's way. God tells them to work out a way of their own somewhere in between.
God tells Israel to keep His statutes and His judgments. What does He say about the man who does these things?

answers.text: He will be rich by them

cards.text: Then comes a long list. God says none of them are to approach any close relative to have sexual relations, and He walks through the family one by one, from mother and sister to aunt and daughter-in-law, then adds a neighbor's wife. Over and over He gives the reason, like it would dishonor a father or shame the family.
This whole list has been about the family. Then God brings up Molech, a god the Ammonites worshiped (1 Kings 11:7), and draws a hard line.

cards.question: What does God say Israel must never give to be sacrificed to Molech?
God says giving a child to Molech would ___ the name of their God.

cards.text: God's still giving Moses His message for Israel. A man must not lie with a man as with a woman, which God calls an abomination, and no one is to lie with an animal, which He calls a perversion.
Now God steps back and looks at the whole list. He says, "Do not defile yourselves by any of these practices," and then He tells them why.

cards.question: God says the ___ He is driving out before Israel have defiled themselves by all these things.
God says even the land has become defiled, and He is punishing it for its sin. What will the land do to its inhabitants?

cards.text: Friend, I got slid into the back of a junk drawer for YEARS, and even that drawer never tried to spit me out. Then God says it plainly: Israel is to keep His statutes and ordinances and not commit any of these abominations.

cards.question: God says only the native-born Israelites must keep these rules, not the foreigner who lives among them.

cards.text: Then God reminds them: the men who were in the land before them committed all these abominations, and the land became defiled.

cards.question: Since God is bringing Israel into the land, He says it will never vomit them out, no matter what they do there.
What does God say must happen to anyone who commits any of these abominations?

answers.text: He must be cut off from his people
He must offer a lamb at the altar
He must stay outside the camp a week

cards.question: God wraps up by telling Israel to keep His charge and stay away from the customs practiced before them. Why does He say to stay away from them?

answers.text: So they do not defile themselves
So the nations will fear them

cards.text: That's where this message lands, friend. But God's not done teaching His people what it looks like to be His, so keep that apron on.

findings.problem: The card says the whole list has been about the family. Card 6 already names a neighbor's wife (18:20), and 18:19 is about a woman during her menstrual period. Neither is about family, so the claim isn't true to the text.

rule.text: **Noticing:** What he points out must be true.

findings.problem: The question asks the baker to finish the wording of the line "the man who does these things will live by them." The answers are word swaps in the same frame: live, rich or rule "by them." Nothing earlier lets the baker reason out the word "live," so this tests wording, not meaning.

rule.text: **Never ask the baker to guess the next words of a line.**

findings.problem: The card opens with a Bible fact from outside the passage, "God's been teaching Israel how His people are to live," but gives no reference for it.

rule.text: **References.** Every Bible fact he states carries its reference.

findings.problem: The list of forbidden practices runs from 18:6 to 18:23. The walkthrough treats 18:6-20 as a long stretch with one summary card (stop 1, card 6). It then gives 18:21 (Molech) two choice cards, and sums up 18:22-23 on a separate story card in stop 2 with no choice cards. If 18:6-23 is one long stretch, it should get one summary card and no choice cards. If these verses are key laws that carry the heart of a sermon titled after these practices, they should get choice cards like anything else. Splitting them this way follows neither reading cleanly.
findings.question: In Leviticus 18, is the list of forbidden practices (18:6-23) a long stretch to sum up in one card, or key laws that get story and choice cards? And if it is a stretch, can a single law inside it, like the Molech law in 18:21, get choice cards?
